subject: Week 21: decide puree vs baby-led weaning before solids start
bodyText:
This week
Days 145-151 are pre-6-month consolidation: supported sitting is steadier, with brief independent moments for some - the CDC sits-without-support checkpoint is 9 months, so support is still the norm. Rolling is now navigation, babble turn-taking sustains several exchanges, and he anticipates outcomes, smiling when the bath starts running. One epidemiological note: ear-infection incidence starts climbing from 6 months, usually riding on viral colds.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Drool surge ahead of the first tooth - eruption typically lands at 6-10 months.
- [monitor] Ear-tugging without other illness signs - usually self-soothing or teething, occasionally early ear pain; watch for the fever pairing.
- [call within 24h] Ear-tugging plus fever plus fussiness - possible otitis media; peak incidence runs 6-24 months.
- [call now] Fever of 102F rectal or higher with lethargy, persistent vomiting with reduced wet diapers, labored breathing, or blue lips - 911 for breathing or color change.

Enrichment opportunities
- Decide the solids method and stage the gear. Combo approaches are common and not harmful, and baby-led weaning does not increase choking risk versus purees in the randomized data - allergen timing matters more than method. Equipment: high chair, bibs, pre-loaded spoons, suction bowl, 2-oz silicone freezer cups, mat under the chair. First 5 foods: avocado, banana, sweet potato, iron-fortified oatmeal, well-cooked egg yolk - then peanut within the first two weeks of solids. AAP - Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Log 30+ minutes outside daily - grass and sand under his hands, birdsong, traffic, wind, and light variation are the sensory curriculum at this age, free of charge.
- Introduce cause-and-effect toys - a ball that rolls when pushed, a button that triggers music. This is the front edge of intentional action-outcome learning.
- Use the final free-tier weeks at La Petite Baleen (933 Mason St) - the free infant-swim window ends when paid tuition starts at 6 months, around day 180. La Petite Baleen - tuition: https://www.swimlpb.com/swim-classes/tuition
- Bank skipped or short naps into an earlier bedtime - 30-60 minutes forward - rather than a late-afternoon make-up nap that pushes the whole night later. AAP - Getting Your Baby to Sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 168-182 (Oct 26-Nov 9, 2026): 6-month well visit - final booking check; solids-readiness assessment and iron/hemoglobin screen happen here.
- Day 166-172 (week of Oct 24, 2026): likely first-solids week if the visit lands early and readiness signs are in - first-foods brief to follow.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Uses voice to express joy and displeasure
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Distinct vocalizations for different states — early affective communication.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-voice-for-joy/complete

- Rolls from back to tummy
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Harder direction; requires more core and upper-body strength.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/rolls-back-to-tummy/complete

- Reaches for objects with one hand
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Differentiation from earlier two-handed swiping — emerging hand preference is normal but unstable until ~age 3.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/reaches-with-one-hand/complete

- Pushes up with straight arms during tummy time
  AAP window: day 120-180
  What to look for: Full arm extension, chest off the floor. Builds toward sitting.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/leans-on-hands-tummy-time/complete

- Leans on hands to support self when sitting
  AAP window: day 120-180
  What to look for: Tripod sit. Precedes hands-free sitting by 1-2 months.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/sits-with-hand-support/complete
